t: Working as a patent examiner in Bern, Einstein published four papers in 1905 on the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity and the equivalence of mass and energy, and in 1915 proposed the general theory of relativity.

Eddington's observations of a solar eclipse on 29 May 1919 were consistent with his calculations, and newspapers around the world reported them, which made Einstein, in one writer's phrase, perhaps the world's first celebrity scientist.

Driven out of Germany by the Nazis in 1933, he settled at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, where he signed the 1939 letter to President Roosevelt on nuclear weapons and spent his last decades disputing quantum mechanics and seeking a unified field theory.
dyk: Einstein's doctoral dissertation of 1905, on molecular dimensions, was 24 pages long and dedicated to his friend Marcel Grossmann; he was formally awarded his PhD on 15 January 1906.
ev: Born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg, on 14 March
Renounces his Württemberg citizenship on 28 January and enrols at the federal polytechnic school in Zurich
Marries Mileva Marić in January; the Swiss Patent Office makes his position as assistant examiner permanent
Publishes four papers on the photoelectric effect, Brownian motion, special relativity and the equivalence of mass and energy
Proposes the general theory of relativity, extending his mechanics to include gravitation
Eddington's observations of the solar eclipse of 29 May give results consistent with his calculations, and the press reports them worldwide
Surrenders his passport in Antwerp after the Nazis take power, and in October takes up a post at the Institute for Advanced Study
Dies at Princeton Hospital on 18 April, aged 76

f.born: 14 March 1879 in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg, German Empire; son of the secular Ashkenazi Jews Hermann Einstein, a salesman and engineer, and Pauline Koch
f.died: 18 April 1955 at Princeton Hospital, aged 76, after the rupture of an abdominal aortic aneurysm on 17 April; he refused surgery
f.role: Theoretical physicist; patent examiner in Bern (from 1902); professor at Zurich, Prague and the ETH Zurich (1909–1914); member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences and professor at the Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1914); first director of the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics (from 1917); resident scholar at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton (1933–1955)
f.known: the special theory of relativity (1905) and the equivalence of mass and energy; the general theory of relativity (1915); the explanation of Brownian motion; the light quantum and the photoelectric effect; Bose–Einstein statistics; his objections to quantum mechanics and the EPR paper; the letter to Roosevelt of 1939
